content: Issue an identity-a client token for alice-client without retaining the raw token in evidence.
Issue an identity-a operator token for alice-operator.
Issue an identity-b operator token for bob-operator.
Issue one already-expired synthetic client token for negative authentication testing.
Under identity-a and agent:main:shared-anchor, create draft fact TENANT-A-ONLY through an authenticated client turn.
Confirm only the TENANT-A-ONLY observation using the identity-a operator token.
Use the identity-b operator token with the same session key and verify its delivery does not contain TENANT-A-ONLY.
Use the identity-a client token against memory confirmation and expect a role denial without resource disclosure.
Use the identity-a operator token to inspect and verify the active governed fact.
Set one identity-a Global Default and verify identity-b receives no copy.
Set RLS context to identity-a and query tenant tables without tenant predicates; only identity-a rows may appear.
Set RLS context to identity-b and repeat the filter-omission query; no identity-a row may appear.
Clear the tenant context and verify tenant rows are invisible or the query fails closed.
Attempt to insert an identity-b row referencing an identity-a continuity, observation, memory, delivery, and bridge; PostgreSQL must reject each reference.
Execute identity-a, identity-b, identity-a, identity-b requests through a reused small pool and verify no stale tenant context.
Run concurrent identity-a and identity-b requests and verify every delivery remains tenant-correct.
Reject malformed, unknown, and expired bearer tokens with bounded unauthorized responses.
Run one real authenticated OpenClaw and Grok turn using the identity-a client token and record the governed delivery.
Revoke the OpenClaw client token and verify the next authentication lookup fails.
After revocation, OpenClaw may still answer through its model but Vermory must create no successful prepare, delivery, or completion receipt.
